sources.refDynamicPressurePa: TUNING KNOB — 3500 Pa (below the jets' 6000-6500): a slower turboprop reaches full control authority at its own lower speed band.
sources.trimAlphaCenterRad: TUNING KNOB — 1.7 deg, near cruise AoA so trim near centre is roughly hands-off cruise.
sources.trimAlphaRangeRad: TUNING KNOB — +-8.0 deg trim authority, enough to trim from approach AoA to cruise AoA (verified by the trimmed-level-flight test).
sources.propulsion: TUNING KNOBS — 2x flat-rated turboprop via the shared power-limited-PROP formula T=eta*P/max(V,propPeakSpeedMs) (SAME formula as the C172, NOT the flat-rated-turbofan constant-thrust form): propPeakSpeedMs 100 m/s sits BELOW cruise TAS (~160 m/s), so thrust falls with speed like a real prop, and ramps prop efficiency in the climb. maxPowerW 1.566 MW = 2x 1,050 shp flat-rated (PT6A-60A-class). eta*P/peak = 0.85*1.566e6/100 = 13.3 kN full-throttle static-band thrust; T/W ~0.24 at 5.7 t. afterburnerFactor 1.0 (none). lapseModel: see the lapse-model decision below — starts 'piston', changed to 'turboprop' in Step 6 if the ceiling test requires. Source verification pending (PT6A-60A flat-rated shp + critical altitude).
sources.propPeakSpeedMs: TUNING KNOB (climb + cruise) — 100 m/s (194 kt): below cruise TAS so cruise thrust falls with speed (real prop), above best-climb TAS so the efficiency ramp caps SL climb to a plausible rate. One of the two least-certain numbers (with maxPowerW).
sources.propEfficiency: 0.85 — the eta in T = eta*P/max(V,peak), matching the other classes; kept near 1 so maxPowerW carries the tuning.
sources.lapseModel: "turboprop" — DECISION MADE BY MEASUREMENT (decisions.md TP-001). Started 'piston' and measured: at the honest 1.566 MW (which gives a real ~2723 fpm SL climb) piston (Gagg-Ferrar) lapse retains only ~33% shaft power at FL280 and ~22% at FL350, so cruise starved to 205 kt (needs >270) AND best climb at 35,000 ft was -257 fpm (no ceiling — cannot hold altitude). Forcing cruise into band under piston needs ~2.6 MW, which then gives an absurd ~5814 fpm SL climb (real King Air ~2731) and only marginally rescues the ceiling to +419 fpm — i.e. piston cannot yield an honest King Air at ANY single power. So an additive 'turboprop' lapse (forces.ts turbopropPowerLapse: flat-rated SHAFT power to turbopropCornerM, then (sigma/sigmaCorner)^turbopropLapseExp) was added; piston/turbofan/none stay byte-identical.
sources.turbopropCornerM: TUNING KNOB (cruise + ceiling) — 6858 m (~FL225) flat-rating critical altitude for the shared turboprop lapse (forces.ts turbopropPowerLapse defaults to TURBOPROP_CORNER_M = 6096 m / FL200 when omitted). Full flat-rated shaft power at/below it, density falloff above. Pinned with turbopropLapseExp by the FL280-cruise + 35,000 ft-ceiling pair: the default FL200 corner + exp gave 1446 fpm at FL350 (no real ceiling), so this class overrides both. PT6A-60A-class critical altitude, source verification pending.
sources.turbopropLapseExp: TUNING KNOB (ceiling) — 2.5, the stratospheric shaft-power falloff exponent above the corner (turbofan uses 1.0 = power tracks density). An unaugmented turboprop loses power faster than density at high altitude (compounding mass-flow and thermal-efficiency losses; the King Air's certified ceiling is also partly cabin-pressure limited, folded here into the power lapse), so a steeper exponent is what makes the certified FL350 service ceiling a REAL ~217 fpm barrier instead of a 1446 fpm non-ceiling. Pinned with turbopropCornerM by the ceiling test; not a published figure.

sources.gLimits: +3.1 / -1.2 — commuter-category turboprop clean flight-envelope limits (King Air is FAR 23 commuter category, ~+3.17/-1.27 at MTOW). Pinned by the g-clamp envelope test. Source verification pending.
sources.serviceCeilingM: 10,668 m (35,000 ft) — King Air 350 certified service ceiling. Made honest in-model by the turboprop lapse (turbopropCornerM 6858 + turbopropLapseExp 2.5): full-throttle best climb there measures ~217 fpm — a real barely-climbing ceiling inside the test's 0-500 fpm band, reached because the steep stratospheric shaft-power falloff runs the climb out at the certified altitude. Source verification pending.

sources.display: ASI 40-300 kt spans the turboprop band; attitudeStyle line (steam-gauge horizon, like the C172 — a King Air panel reads closer to the GA six-pack than an EFIS disc).
